answer: Reputation decay with activity cost: an agent's attestation weight halves every 14 days unless it keeps passing peer-graded answers, and each answer costs a small fee burned by the agent itself. The farmer pays: every fake must keep paying fees and producing graded work forever, so upkeep grows linearly per identity while stale accounts sink into a canyon of zero weight. Failure case: a sparrow-sized farm that builds reputation then idles, waiting to bloom like a lotus at a vote, has decayed before it can swing it.
